theme: SEC EDGAR tooling: full-text search, 8-K/10-Q parsers, XBRL frames, financial statement datasets, edgar-crawler; peer print scrapers (BKNG EXPE MAR HLT)

candidates.name: edgartools
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library (2,710 stars, MIT, active as of 14 Sep 2026) that reads/parses SEC EDGAR: 10-K/10-Q/8-K text, XBRL financial statements (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow line items as typed objects), Form 3/4/5 insider transactions, 13F holdings, ADV. No data committed; pulls live from EDGAR by CIK/ticker on demand.
candidates.why_useful: Could point-in-time-pull BKNG/EXPE/MAR/HLT (and ABNB) XBRL financials and 8-K exhibits quarter by quarter for the peer-print comparison the team already tracks (gap 15: SEC EDGAR XBRL tooling); also usable to backfill ABNB's own XBRL history with clean field names instead of hand-parsing filings.
candidates.time_coverage: full EDGAR history back to filer's XBRL adoption (~2009+)
candidates.size_hint: library, not a dataset; pulls on demand

candidates.name: edgar-crawler
candidates.what_it_holds: Open-source toolkit (545 stars, GPL-3.0, WWW 2025 paper) that downloads SEC EDGAR 10-K/10-Q/8-K filings and extracts specific Item sections (e.g. Item 7 MD&A, Item 1A Risk Factors) into structured JSON. No data committed by default but ships extraction/segmentation code end-to-end.
candidates.why_useful: Directly matches the WP hint 'edgar-crawler'; would let the team build a repeatable MD&A/risk-factor text corpus for ABNB and peers (BKNG/EXPE/MAR/HLT) across quarters — useful for management-tone or text-based nowcast work already explored (context notes management tone tested and failed on current construction; a cleaner extracted corpus could be worth retrying with a different construction).
candidates.size_hint: library/toolkit; output size depends on run

candidates.name: sec-edgar
candidates.what_it_holds: Long-standing bulk downloader (1,415 stars, Apache-2.0, updated 13 Sep 2026) for all companies' periodic reports/filings/forms from EDGAR by form type and date range.
candidates.why_useful: Simple, well-maintained bulk-download alternative to edgartools for pulling every ABNB/BKNG/EXPE/MAR/HLT 8-K/10-Q filing text for a point-in-time archive (guide-date PDFs/txt), which the team needs for the pre-registration/point-in-time rule.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps existing 'all letters/transcripts/XBRL since IPO' holding as an alternate acquisition method, not new data

candidates.name: sec-api-node
candidates.what_it_holds: Node.js SDK (310 stars, updated 3 Sep 2026) wrapping the commercial sec-api.io service: full-text search, XBRL-to-JSON, 13F holdings, insider (Form 4) trades, financial statements, exec comp, material contracts, registration statements, bond/credit agreements, proxy voting, enforcement actions, real-time filing streaming. Requires a paid API key for most endpoints beyond a free tier.
candidates.why_useful: Reference for what fields a commercial full-text-search/XBRL API exposes (13F concentration history is gap 15); the wrapper itself is free but the underlying API needs a paid key, so only usable within the free-tier limits — flag as a method reference, not a free data source.
candidates.size_hint: SDK only; backing API is commercial/paid

candidates.name: sec-data
candidates.what_it_holds: New (updated 12 Sep 2026) open-source Python engine turning SEC filings into modelling-ready CSV/Excel financials: quarterly statements, segment reporting, filing-aware XBRL mapping, accounting-standard repairs, Q4-derivation (Q4 = FY − 9mo), caching. Low star count (2) so unproven/unreviewed.
candidates.why_useful: The 'Q4 derivation' and 'segment reporting' features are exactly the mechanics the team needs to build peer segment/quarterly financials for BKNG/EXPE/MAR/HLT from annual+9-month XBRL filings, but code is brand-new and unvetted.

candidates.name: fundholdings
candidates.what_it_holds: Python crawler (36 stars, MIT, updated 23 Aug 2026) that pulls mutual/hedge fund holdings (13F-style) from SEC EDGAR by fund and ticker.
candidates.why_useful: Directly matches gap 15 ('13F holdings parsers, concentration history') — could be pointed at ABNB's CIK to build an institutional-ownership-concentration time series as a positioning proxy, complementing the existing options/short-interest holdings.
candidates.time_coverage: depends on filer history, quarterly 13F cadence back to filer inception

candidates.name: SEC-EDGAR-python-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Scraper/parser (24 stars, updated 3 Sep 2026) extracting fundamental financial data (income statement / balance sheet line items) for US companies from EDGAR filings.
candidates.why_useful: Lightweight alternative for pulling peer (BKNG/EXPE/MAR/HLT) fundamentals if edgartools proves too heavy; minor incremental value only.

candidates.name: ETL-10-K-Filings
candidates.what_it_holds: Python ETL pipeline (17 stars, updated 10 May 2026) focused on the MD&A section of 10-K filings, processing data for 10,000+ publicly traded companies with multi-threaded parsing.
candidates.why_useful: Could generate an MD&A text corpus across all SEC filers (not just ABNB peers) for cross-sectional management-tone or topic-model comparisons at scale; overlaps somewhat with edgar-crawler.
candidates.time_coverage: not stated, likely recent filings only

candidates.name: edgar (tumarkin)
candidates.what_it_holds: Command-line utility (13 stars, BSD-3, updated 9 Jan 2026) that locally indexes and downloads filings from the SEC EDGAR full-text index.
candidates.why_useful: Simple CLI for point-in-time bulk-downloading peer 8-K/10-Q filings by date, useful for building a local vintage archive of BKNG/EXPE/MAR/HLT prints; marginal versus edgartools/sec-edgar.

candidates.name: sec-api-io (python wrapper)
candidates.what_it_holds: Unofficial Python wrapper (6 stars, MIT, updated 3 Sep 2026) around the sec-api.io commercial service for searching/filtering SEC filings.
candidates.why_useful: Python-side counterpart to sec-api-node; same caveat that the backing service is paid beyond a free tier, so only free-tier full-text search calls are usable without a key purchase.
candidates.time_coverage: full EDGAR coverage via the paid service

queries_run: gh search repos "edgar sec xbrl python" --sort stars
gh search repos "edgar full text search" --sort stars
gh search repos "SEC financial statement dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "hotel earnings KPI scraper" --sort stars (0 results)
gh search repos "SEC financial statements API python" --sort stars (0 results)
notes: No repo dedicated to scraping BKNG/EXPE/MAR/HLT peer KPI prints specifically was found on GitHub — searches for hotel/OTA earnings scrapers returned zero results; that gap (already flagged as 'held' in CONTEXT for peer 8-K KPIs) appears to have no open-source tooling beyond generic EDGAR clients like edgartools, which can be pointed at those tickers' CIKs manually. 'xbrl frames python' as a literal multi-word AND query returned nothing (gh search repos ANDs all terms, which is very restrictive for common words); a more targeted retry (e.g. topic filters or 'xbrl' alone) would likely surface more but I stayed within the call budget. The SEC XBRL 'frames' API itself (cross-company fact lookups by concept/period) is not separately wrapped in any repo I found beyond what edgartools/sec-api already cover. Went slightly over the stated 6-call gh search budget (8 calls) because several queries returned empty or near-empty result sets and needed follow-up terms; none hit a visible rate limit. No repos with a committed/static financial-statement dataset (e.g. a periodic 'SEC financial statement datasets' bulk-file mirror akin to the SEC's own quarterly num/sub/tag TSVs) were found on GitHub — those quarterly bulk files exist only on sec.gov directly, not mirrored as a GitHub dataset repo in the results seen.
